description: Browse the world object catalog with optional filters, or reverse-lookup a single item by GUID. Prerequisite: none — this is a read-only catalog query; no lot access or build permission required. Effect: returns a filtered, sorted list of purchaseable items from Content.WorldCatalog. By default restricted to the server's roommate whitelist (categories 12..20). Cost: none — no simoleon debit, no PDU emitted. Filters: guid_hex (reverse-lookup of a single catalog entry by hex GUID — accepts BOTH the catalog GUID and any subordinate instance GUID a multitile object spawns; response includes instance_guid_hex echoing the input and instance_guids listing every OBJD GUID in the iff's multitile group; bypasses category/tier/price/name filters and the whitelist so any object visible on a tile can be resolved), name (substring), category (integer 12..20 or slug: seating/surfaces/appliances/entertainment/skill/decorative/misc/lighting/pets), tier (cheap|mid|expensive — P33/P67 percentile bins over all whitelisted items), min_price, max_price. Limit clamp: max 200 results regardless of the limit arg. Response includes categories_summary listing all categories represented in the filtered result set.

args.name: guid_hex
args.description: Hex GUID to reverse-lookup (e.g. 0x17579980 or 0x1478FD75). Accepts either the catalog GUID (master OBJD; what buy-object expects) OR an instance GUID (subordinate OBJD; what query-lot-objects reports for placed BaseObjects of multitile items). Returns the single matching catalog entry; result has guid_hex=catalog GUID, instance_guid_hex=echo of input, and instance_guids[]=every OBJD GUID in the multitile group. Ignores all other filters; whitelist (categories 12..20) and blacklist are bypassed so non-purchaseable items resolve too.

call_signatures: cf $CF search-catalog --category seating --tier cheap                         # cheap seating items
cf $CF search-catalog --name lamp --tier mid                                  # mid-tier lamps
cf $CF search-catalog --guid_hex 0x17579980                                   # reverse-lookup by catalog GUID
cf $CF search-catalog --guid_hex 0x1478FD75                                   # reverse-lookup by INSTANCE GUID (the one query-lot-objects reports)
common_mistakes: category outside whitelist (12..20) returns 0 results, not an error.
limit > 200 is silently clamped to 200 server-side.
tier=cheap/mid/expensive uses P33/P67 percentile bins computed lazily at first call — bins are snapshot-relative to the loaded catalog.
category accepts both integers (14) and slugs (appliances) — use list-catalog-categories to discover available slugs.
guid_hex must be a 32-bit hex value (with or without 0x prefix); malformed values return an error, unknown GUIDs return count:0.
Multi-tile items (beds, dressers, large rugs) have a catalog GUID that differs from the instance GUID query-lot-objects reports; pass either — both resolve to the same catalog entry.
perception_hints: Use search-catalog before buy-object to pick a GUID you can afford: filter by max_price=<your balance>.
Use list-catalog-categories first to see which categories have items.
Use --guid_hex when query-lot-objects shows a GUID you don't recognise — it bypasses the whitelist so non-purchaseable items resolve too.

If you see a placed multitile object on a tile (bed, dresser, large rug), the GUID in query-lot-objects is the INSTANCE GUID, not the catalog GUID. --guid_hex resolves both — use the response's guid_hex field if you want to buy or move another copy.
